bib.title: Knowledge Fusion of Large Language Models

question: Can the knowledge of several structurally different LLMs be fused into one target LLM by distilling their combined next-token distributions through light continual training?
hypothesis: After fusion the target model will surpass any of the source models in performance.
contributions: Introduce knowledge fusion of LLMs: externalise the knowledge of multiple source LLMs via their generative distributions and transfer it to a target LLM
Token alignment by minimum edit distance (MinED) and two fusion functions (MinCE, AvgCE)
Experiments with Llama-2, OpenLLaMA and MPT on 42 tasks (reasoning, commonsense, code), plus comparison with ensemble and weight merging

method.summary: Run K source LLMs on each MiniPile text, align their token-level distribution matrices (MinED), fuse them (MinCE picks the source with lowest cross-entropy to the gold tokens), and continually train a Llama-2 7B target with L = lambda*L_CLM + (1-lambda)*L_Fusion, lambda 0.9. Evaluated on BBH, Common Sense and MultiPL-E.
method.task: multi-teacher distillation by continual pre-training (knowledge fusion)

datasets.size: about 1 million documents, 22 domains, 1.8 billion tokens
datasets.source: curated from The Pile by E5-Large embeddings, K-means clustering and cluster filtering
datasets.preprocessing: sequence packing with EOS separators; max length 2048

models.name: Llama-2 7B
models.init_from: target starts from the same pre-trained Llama-2 7B weights as the source

other.use: teacher for the Llama-2 KD baseline

training.objective: L = lambda*L_CLM + (1-lambda)*L_Fusion, lambda = 0.9 (static); L_Fusion divergence between target distribution Q_t and fused P_t; MinCE fusion default
training.tokens: inferred: about 1.57B tokens per Fig 2 x-axis end for the BBH curve; MiniPile is 1.8B tokens
training.hardware: single node, 8 NVIDIA A100 GPUs, 40GB each

other.divergence_D: not named in Sec 3 beyond KL being equivalent to CLM; Eq 4 leaves D abstract
other.teacher_forward_passes: source distributions computed for every training text; storage or on-the-fly not stated

baselines: Llama-2 CLM (continued training on MiniPile with CLM only)
eval.protocol: Single training run per configuration; no seeds, variance or significance tests reported. Relative improvements are computed against Llama-2 7B.

evidence.quote: MiniPile comprises approximately 1 million documents across 22 domains and 1.8 billion tokens

results.claim: FuseLLM improves Big-Bench Hard average (27 tasks, few-shot CoT, exact match) by 5.16% relative over Llama-2 7B.
results.setup: Target Llama-2 7B, sources Llama-2 7B + OpenLLaMA 7B + MPT 7B, MinCE fusion, MinED alignment, lambda 0.9, continual training 1 epoch on MiniPile (1.8B tokens), single run
results.quote: FUSELLM demonstrates an average relative performance gain of 5.16% over the original Llama-2 across all 27 tasks

results.claim: Absolute BBH average: FuseLLM 41.75 vs Llama-2 39.70 (about 2.05 points).
results.setup: Target Llama-2 7B, sources Llama-2 7B + OpenLLaMA 7B + MPT 7B, MinCE fusion, MinED alignment, lambda 0.9, continual training 1 epoch on MiniPile (1.8B tokens), single run
results.table: Table 1, row Avg. 27 Tasks, column FUSELLM

results.setup: Llama-2 7B continually trained on MiniPile with CLM loss only
results.quote: Llama-2 CLM shows a relative improvement of 1.86% compared to Llama-2

results.claim: Distilling from a single Llama-2 13B into Llama-2 7B gives +2.97% relative on BBH, below FuseLLM's 5.16%.
results.setup: Llama-2 KD: conventional KD from Llama-2 13B (47.92 BBH) to Llama-2 7B, same MiniPile corpus; BBH 40.88 vs 41.75
results.note: Llama-2 13B itself scores 47.92 on BBH, far above all 7B models including FuseLLM
results.quote: especially in the case of BBH (2.97% vs. 5.16%)

results.claim: On Common Sense (5 zero-shot likelihood tasks) FuseLLM gains 1.25% relative over Llama-2.
results.setup: Target Llama-2 7B, sources Llama-2 7B + OpenLLaMA 7B + MPT 7B, MinCE fusion, MinED alignment, lambda 0.9, continual training 1 epoch on MiniPile (1.8B tokens), single run
results.quote: achieving a relative performance improvement of 1.25% over Llama-2

results.claim: On MultiPL-E (10 languages, pass@1, 20 samples) FuseLLM gains 6.36% relative over Llama-2 but still trails OpenLLaMA and MPT.
results.setup: Target Llama-2 7B, sources Llama-2 7B + OpenLLaMA 7B + MPT 7B, MinCE fusion, MinED alignment, lambda 0.9, continual training 1 epoch on MiniPile (1.8B tokens), single run

limits: Single run per configuration, no seeds or variance; several ablation gaps (EM vs MinED, static vs dynamic lambda) are 0.0 to 0.7 points.

Target is the strongest source (Llama-2) on BBH and CS, but on code Llama-2 is the weakest of the three, and FuseLLM still trails OpenLLaMA and MPT on MultiPL-E; authors blame the low code share of MiniPile (approx 7.59%).
FuseLLM degrades on some tasks (Geometric Shapes, Word Sorting) because other sources do poorly there.
The 13B KD baseline is stronger than any source (BBH 47.92) yet FuseLLM at 7B scale is the only one compared with it on gains, not absolute scores.
Fusion needs source logits for every training token and a MinED alignment across tokenizers.
Same-architecture comparison with ensemble and weight merging uses only Pythia 1B and perplexity, no downstream tasks.
Cost of computing source distributions is not reported.
